title: Nanasaheb Peshwa
subtitle: From the Narmada to Attock, and the catastrophe at Panipat · 1740 – 1761
subject: nanasaheb
intro: Balaji Bajirao, known as Nanasaheb, was Peshwa for 21 years. Under him the Marathas became the dominant power across most of India: Pune replaced Satara as the centre of government, Maratha armies collected tribute from Bengal to the Punjab, and in 1758 they reached Attock on the Indus. The overreach ended in 1761 at Panipat, one of the bloodiest battles of the century.

events.title: Malwa formally granted
events.summary: Through Jai Singh's mediation the emperor Muhammad Shah names the Peshwa deputy governor of Malwa — imperial recognition of what Bajirao had won by force.

events.title: Bhaskar Pant murdered in Bengal
events.summary: Alivardi Khan invites Raghuji Bhonsle's general Bhaskar Pant to talks and has him and his officers killed; the Bhonsle raids on Bengal grow fiercer.

events.title: Bengal pays chauth; Orissa ceded
events.summary: After a decade of raids Alivardi Khan agrees to pay chauth for Bengal and cedes Orissa to the Bhonsles of Nagpur.

events.title: The Sangola agreement
events.summary: At Sangola the young Chhatrapati Rajaram II confirms the Peshwa's control of the administration; the Peshwa's Pune becomes the real capital of the empire.

events.title: Treaty of Bhalki with the Nizam
events.summary: War with the Nizam's son Salabat Jung, backed by the French under Bussy, ends with the Treaty of Bhalki and Maratha gains in Khandesh and Berar.

events.title: Abdali invades again
events.summary: Ahmad Shah Abdali crosses the Indus once more to drive the Marathas out of the Punjab; Najib ud-Daula and the Rohillas join him.

events.title: Bhau takes Delhi
events.summary: Sadashivrao Bhau occupies Delhi and strips the silver ceiling of the Diwan-i-Khas to pay his unpaid army.

events.title: Entrenched at Panipat
events.summary: The two armies dig in facing each other at Panipat. Abdali cuts the Maratha supply lines and two months of hunger follow.

events.title: "Two pearls dissolved"
events.summary: News of Panipat reaches Nanasaheb near Bhilsa in a coded letter: two pearls dissolved, twenty-seven gold coins lost, silver and copper beyond counting — Vishwasrao and Bhau dead.

events.title: Balaji Bajirao born
events.summary: Nanasaheb is born to Bajirao I and Kashibai, the year his father becomes Peshwa.

events.title: Becomes Peshwa at 19
events.summary: Shahu appoints Nanasaheb Peshwa after Bajirao's sudden death. Unlike his father he is above all an administrator and a financier.

events.title: Maratha invasions of Bengal
events.summary: Raghuji Bhonsle of Nagpur raids Bengal year after year — the 'bargi' raids remembered in Bengali lullabies. In 1751 Nawab Alivardi Khan agrees to pay chauth and cedes the revenue of Orissa.

events.title: Shahu dies; power moves to Pune
events.summary: Shahu dies childless and Tarabai's 'grandson' Ramaraja becomes Chhatrapati. In 1750, at Sangola, the Peshwa takes over the administration of the state and the government departments move to Pune.

events.title: Tarabai's revolt
events.summary: Tarabai imprisons Ramaraja and, with the Gaekwads, challenges the Peshwa. Nanasaheb defeats Damaji Gaekwad and comes to terms with Tarabai, who keeps Satara fort but loses real influence.

events.title: Protectors of the Mughal emperor
events.summary: By an agreement with the Mughal court, the Marathas undertake to defend the emperor against internal and foreign enemies — chiefly the Afghans — in return for revenue rights in the north-west. It draws them deep into north Indian politics.

events.title: Siege of Kumher
events.summary: Raghunathrao and Malharrao Holkar besiege the Jat fort of Kumher. Malharrao's son Khanderao is killed, and his widow Ahilyabai later becomes the ruler of Indore.

events.title: Destruction of the Angre fleet
events.summary: In alliance with the British East India Company, the Peshwa attacks Tulaji Angre. A British squadron destroys the Maratha fleet at Vijaydurg — removing the Maratha navy, with long-term consequences.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: In Bengal, Robert Clive's victory over Siraj-ud-Daulah makes the East India Company a territorial power — a development the Marathas, focused on the north-west, do not yet treat as their main threat.

events.title: Raghunathrao takes Delhi
events.summary: Raghunathrao and Malharrao Holkar expel the Afghan-backed Najib-ud-Daula from Delhi, putting the city under Maratha influence.

events.title: Marathas at Attock and Peshawar
events.summary: Raghunathrao's army drives Abdali's Afghan governors out of Lahore and reaches Attock and Peshawar — the furthest point of Maratha expansion. The gains are not held.

events.title: Dattaji Shinde killed at Burari Ghat
events.summary: Abdali returns to India. Dattaji Shinde, holding the north, is killed fighting the Afghans and Najib at Burari Ghat near Delhi. His last words are remembered as 'Bachenge to aur bhi ladenge' — 'if we survive, we shall fight again'.

events.title: Battle of Udgir
events.summary: Sadashivrao Bhau defeats the Nizam's army at Udgir, winning major territory and forts in the Deccan. His prestige leads to his being given command of the northern expedition.

events.title: Bhau marches north
events.summary: A large Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau, with the Peshwa's son Vishwasrao, leaves for the north, accompanied by a huge train of non-combatants and pilgrims. It takes Delhi in August.

events.title: Battle of Kunjpura
events.summary: The Marathas storm Abdali's depot at Kunjpura, but Abdali crosses the Yamuna behind them and cuts their supply line to the south. Both armies dig in near Panipat.

events.title: Third Battle of Panipat
events.summary: After two months of starvation in their entrenched camp, the Marathas attack. The battle is close until midday, but Vishwasrao is killed, Bhau disappears in the fighting, and the army collapses. Tens of thousands of soldiers and camp followers are killed or enslaved. Ibrahim Khan Gardi is captured and executed.

events.title: Nanasaheb dies at Parvati
events.summary: Broken by the news from Panipat, Nanasaheb dies at Parvati in Pune, aged 40. His 16-year-old son Madhavrao succeeds him.
